claim: Few-shot LLMs formalise only a minority of competition or undergraduate statements perfectly: 25.3% (Codex, MATH to Isabelle, N=150), 13.4% (Codex with retrieved prompts, ProofNet Lean 3, N=371), 0% few-shot without retrieval on ProofNet.
agent_test: Count full-correct rate of statement formalisation by our agent vs plain prompt at equal tokens on a held-out 100 problems, human-graded.

claim: Compiling or type-checking is a weak proxy for correctness: typecheck 45.2% vs accuracy 16.1% (ProofNet); Poiroux: type-check correlates r=0.655 with human accuracy across 65 systems, vs 0.974 for BEq+. 2026 update: compile-vs-faithful gap 1.3 to 29.5 points across eight systems (d04); SA-PASS 61.8% compile vs 11.2% aligned on research-level problems (d06).
agent_test: Report both compile rate and independent semantic-equivalence rate; flag gap above 2x as an alarm.

claim: Sampling plus selection gives large gains: GPT-4o 31.0% to 45.1% on ProofNet# (50 samples, type-check, selection); Llemma 7B BEq+ pass@n 4.11% to 40.54% (n=1 to 1000); GPT-4 pass@1 to pass@10 gap 19.5-26.5 points.
agent_test: Compare 1 sample vs k samples with a selector at equal total tokens; check whether selection beats majority vote.

claim: Symbolic-equivalence selection is not clearly better than simple Self-BLEU or majority vote in one study, while another reports symbolic equivalence plus semantic consistency beats baselines; mixed. Matched-call test (4 calls, ProofNet#, DeepSeek V4-Pro): Sample-Filter 131 true successes vs Lean-Retry 131 vs typed-IR 129, a tie (d05).
agent_test: Run both selectors on same sample sets.

claim: Errors are mostly semantic alignment, not syntax: Wu et al. failure counts show definition misalignment (46 of 112 failures across subjects) and wrong function use dominate over syntax errors (20); LINC syntax errors fall with model size (38%, 24%, 13%). 2026 update: for a frontier model (DeepSeek V4-Pro, ProofNet#, n=186) type-only failures (61) outnumber semantic-only failures (16); hallucinated Mathlib identifiers are 34-50% of paraphrase-induced failures; semantic errors dominate only for weaker or one-shot systems and for gold-label errors (d05, d09, d04).
agent_test: Tag failure types in our agent's logs; test a definition-alignment check step.

claim: Informalisation (formal to natural language) is much easier than formalisation: 76% vs 25% (Wu, N=38), 62.3% vs 13.4% (ProofNet, N=371). Back-translation can therefore serve as a round-trip check, but no source here validated it as a correctness test.
agent_test: Test round-trip (formalise, informalise, compare) as a detector of wrong formalisations against human labels.

claim: Retrieval of similar examples helps weak models strongly: ProofNet Codex 13.4 to 16.1 with distilled back-translation (+retrieval from 0 to 13.4); MS-RAG with Mistral 7B beats Mixtral 8x7B fixed-prompt; but fine-tuned MMA and Lean Workbook models did not beat base on RLM25.
agent_test: Retrieve k analogous solved formalisations into the prompt vs none.

claim: Project context matters for research-level formalisation: GPT-4o BEq+ 1.50% (12-shot) vs 20.64% with full file context and 24.56% with context minus proofs on RLM25 (619 pairs). Second and third studies: GPT-4o proof rate 11.72% to 27.08% with file context (miniCTX, d10); dependency retrieval precision/recall 0.8-0.9 vs 0.2-0.5 (d11); LLM+P fails without an example problem (d12). Boundary: true code as context did not help spec writing (Verina, d14).
agent_test: Give the agent the surrounding definitions vs not and compare.

claim: Benchmark quality is a problem: 31.8% (118 of 371) of ProofNet Lean 4 port entries had formalisation errors; Lean Workbook human-sampled accuracy 93.5% while NLI-passing data had more number-theory mistakes; checker false negatives about 15.8% in LeanEuclid.
agent_test: Audit a random 50 of our checker-passed items by hand.

claim: Self-refinement with compiler feedback raises executability but not necessarily accuracy: Logic-LM executable rate up (GPT-3.5 FOLIO 66.7 to 84.3) while accuracy stagnates; binary feedback hurt DeepSeekMath-7B; a critic-in-loop raised human accuracy 38.0 to 54.0 (compiler) to 84.0 (compiler plus CriticLeanGPT, N=100 type sample). Gains from compiler feedback are about 64% type-stratum recovery with semantic errors flat on net (d05); nearly half of an agent compile gain fails the semantic criterion (d04).
agent_test: Compare revise-on-compiler-error vs revise-on-semantic-critic at equal tokens.

claim: Formalising reasoning to a solver helps on rigid logic tasks but not always: LINC ProofWriter GPT-4 98.3%, FOLIO LINC 72.5% vs CoT 75.3% (McNemar p=0.58); Logic-LM GPT-4 PrOntoQA 83.2 below CoT 98.79; SatLM GSM-Sys 69.4 vs CoT 46.5. With reasoning models, formalising underperformed solving in 12 of 16 reasoning-model/dataset pairs and 4 of 8 non-reasoning pairs on constraint tasks (d13); LLM+P wins on planning with a human-written domain file (d12).
agent_test: Route logic-puzzle items to a solver, compare vs CoT on FOLIO-like items.

claim: Errors from LINC/CoT overlap little (similarity 0.14-0.22 vs 0.52-0.56 among in-context methods), so combining symbolic and CoT answers could pay.
agent_test: Combine solver and CoT answers by agreement; measure.

claim: Verifying informal steps by formalisation helps: DTV avg solve 65.0% vs majority vote 61.5% (Minerva 62B) and 68.2% with GPT-3.5 formalising; gains largest on number theory and GSM8K.
agent_test: Formalise-and-check answer step vs majority vote at equal token budget.

claim: Informal proofs as drafts help formal proving even when wrong: DSP 39.3% miniF2F test vs Thor 29.9%; 21 of 50 wrong drafts still gave proofs; removing the automated prover costs 9 points.
agent_test: Compare draft-then-formal-check vs direct proof.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Expert-iteration with autoformalised data improves proving: miniF2F valid/test 28.3/29.9 to 37.3/35.2 after two iterations; large autoformalised corpora (Lean Workbook 57K pairs, Goedel 1.64M, Herald) support open provers, with mixed-style data helping (miniF2F 57.6 vs 56.5).
agent_test: Not applicable without training; use only as motivation.

claim: Real-world definition-heavy text is harder: GPT-4o success 13.78 points lower and first error 31.90 points earlier than on miniF2F-Test.
agent_test: Test our agent on definitions-heavy items separately.

claim: Strong dependence on prompt wording/example: case study wrong without example, perfect after one tangential example; Lean 4 fixed prompts gave none of 15 completions elaborating in one worked example.
agent_test: Vary examples and measure variance.

claim: Learned alignment judges are weak against humans: FormalAlign 65.0% vs GPT-4o 47.5% vs human experts 79.58% on an 80-item sample (kappa 0.49); human agreement itself is moderate. 2025-2026 judges are much stronger: two cross-family LLM judges plus compile agree with the human majority on 54/59 (91.5%) vs 45/59 for a LeanScorer-style rule (d04); SA-PASS 98.8% agreement with experts (d06); LeanScorer F1 0.92 (d01). Human labels are noisy too (held-out reviewer kappa 0.18-0.28, d04; human pairwise agreement about 69-70%, d07).
agent_test: Measure our own LLM-judge agreement with human labels.

claim: Dataset size/quality filters have costs: FormalMATH keeps 72.09% before manual check; semantic voting cut compile-passing 92.4% to 32.7%; best prover 16.46%; so compile-passing statements are mostly not faithful.
agent_test: Estimate faithful fraction of compile-passing outputs by manual audit.

claim: Scores rise quickly with specialised models: Herald 93.2-96.7% miniF2F-test, but graduate-level 22.5-23.5%; ATLAS pass@1 39.46% ProofNet vs Herald 31.43%; the competition benchmark is nearly saturated and gap to textbook level remains.
agent_test: Use harder non-saturated test items.

claim: Round-trip (re-informalise and compare) alone is a weak detector of wrong formalisations: on Gaokao-Formal human labels re-informalisation had precision 93, recall 50, F1 0.65, vs plain LLM judge 73/100/0.85 and a staged scorer 94/89/0.92. Multi-edge consistency checking with one hard formal check had no false accepts on 240 adversarial code variants (Clover). Statutory round trip is validated only against an NLI proxy.
agent_test: Run re-informalisation as a cheap filter and compare with a separate judge on 100 labelled items; report precision and recall, not only accuracy.

claim: Compile pass overstates faithfulness: gap between compiling and judged-faithful outputs 1.3 to 29.5 points across eight systems (227 statements); an agent compiles 87.2% but 57.7% pass; SA-PASS 61.8% compile vs 11.2% aligned. For the newest models most rejections are judge errors (4 of 54 real), so judge-only gating is unreliable at the frontier.
agent_test: Gate on compile AND two judges of different families, with stronger or human review of rejections.

claim: At equal LLM calls, compile-feedback retry, sample-and-filter and typed-IR repair tie on statement formalisation (131/131/129 true successes of 186 vs 95 for one shot). For proofs, verifier-feedback refinement beats independent resampling at matched query counts, but gains saturate on hard items. Token-matched tests are still missing.
agent_test: Test sample-and-filter vs retry at equal tokens on 100 statements, with a human-graded semantic judge.

claim: Frontier-model statement failures in 2026 are mostly elaboration and library errors, not silent weakening: type-only 61 vs semantic-only 16 of 186 (DeepSeek V4-Pro); hallucinated Mathlib identifiers 34-50% of paraphrase failures. Typical semantic slips: hard-coding a field size, Summable for a limit, reversed inequality, dropped hypothesis, iff vs one direction.
schema_part: S2 translate / O check against six error types
agent_test: Checklist at formalisation: objects, conditions, conclusion, logical structure, types, library names.

claim: Reasoning models tend to solve instead of formalise: Claude-4-thinking reasoning traces for training hurt a formaliser because they solved the problem; in constraint problems reasoning models hard-code solutions inside the formal program.
agent_test: Block the formalising state from computing the answer; check the statement has no hard-coded result.

claim: Paraphrase sensitivity: rewording the same theorem changes the Lean output; surface consistency 19.1-49.5% (ProofNet#) and 44.5-55.5% (miniF2F) across four frontier models; where both outputs compile they are nearly equivalent (GTED median at least 0.943).
agent_test: Formalise 3 paraphrases; treat disagreement among compiling outputs as the alarm.

claim: Formalise-then-check works for code specs: nl2postcond postconditions caught 64 real Defects4J bugs; Verina best model o3 gets 72.6% code, 52.3% sound-and-complete spec, 4.9% proof; true spec helps code generation, true code does not help spec generation.
agent_test: Use generated specs as tests before proving.

claim: No direct test of autoformalization contamination on fresh post-cutoff problems was found. Indirect: informal Putnam accuracy drops 19.6 points (46.8% relative) on fresh variants for the best model; miniF2F is saturated; PutnamBench built hard on purpose.
agent_test: Evaluate on freshly written variants, not public benchmarks.

claim: Only one cost figure exists for validated statements: FormalMATH human check at 6.89 USD per statement, 12 annotators, 22 days; no study compares cost at equal faithfulness for an automated pipeline.
agent_test: Log tokens and human minutes per accepted statement.
